classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate reflections, scaling and translations for square-root curves, determine endpoints and direction from the radicand, and calculate intercepts while rejecting those outside the domain or output range.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each of the following functions over their implied domains. Label vertices and axial intercepts with their coordinates.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ left by 2 units. The endpoint is $(-2,0)$, and the curve extends right and upwards.

The radicand requires $x+2\ge0$, so the domain is $[-2,\infty)$.

At $x=0$, $y=\sqrt2$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{x+2}&=0\\x+2&=0\\x&=-2.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(-2,0)$ and $(0,\sqrt2)$.

spec.description: Complete square-root sketch with endpoint and both intercepts; no grid or numeric axis ticks.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ down by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(0,-1)$, and the curve extends right and upwards. The domain is $[0,\infty)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-1$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{x}-1&=0\\\sqrt{x}&=1\\x&=1.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(1,0)$ and $(0,-1)$.

spec.description: Increasing square-root curve with endpoint on the negative y-axis and labelled x-intercept.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ right by 2 units. The endpoint is $(2,0)$, and the curve extends right and upwards.

The radicand requires $x-2\ge0$, so the domain is $[2,\infty)$.

At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{x-2}&=0\\x-2&=0\\x&=2.\end{align*}$$
There is no $y$-intercept because $x=0$ is outside the domain.

spec.description: Square-root curve beginning at (2,0), wholly to the right of the y-axis.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ up by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(0,1)$, and the curve extends right and upwards. The domain is $[0,\infty)$.

At $x=0$, $y=1$. Since $\sqrt{x}+1\ge1$, there is no $x$-intercept.

spec.description: Square-root curve beginning at (0,1), with no x-intercept.

answer.short:
Endpoint and $y$-intercept $(0,-1)$; $x$-intercept $(\tfrac14,0)$. Domain $[0,\infty)$.

Dilate vertically by factor 2, then translate down 1 unit.
answer.worked:
Dilate $y=\sqrt{x}$ vertically by factor 2, then translate down by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(0,-1)$, and the curve extends right and upwards. The domain is $[0,\infty)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-1$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}2\sqrt{x}-1&=0\\2\sqrt{x}&=1\\\sqrt{x}&=\tfrac12\\x&=\tfrac14.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(\tfrac14,0)$ and $(0,-1)$.

spec.description: Vertically dilated square-root curve; separate labels for the closely spaced endpoint and x-intercept.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in the $x$-axis, then translate up by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(0,1)$, and the curve extends right and downwards. The domain is $[0,\infty)$.

At $x=0$, $y=1$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}-\sqrt{x}+1&=0\\\sqrt{x}&=1\\x&=1.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$.

spec.description: Decreasing square-root curve from (0,1), crossing at (1,0).

answer.short: Endpoint and both axial intercepts $(0,0)$. Domain $(-\infty,0]$.
answer.worked:
Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in the $y$-axis. The endpoint is $(0,0)$, and the curve extends left and upwards.

The radicand requires $-x\ge0$, so the domain is $(-\infty,0]$. Setting either $x=0$ or $y=0$ gives the common axial intercept $(0,0)$.

spec.description: Square-root curve extending into quadrant II from the origin.

answer.short:
Endpoint and $y$-intercept $(0,-1)$; no $x$-intercept. Domain $(-\infty,0]$.

Reflect in both axes, then translate down 1 unit.
answer.worked:
Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in both axes, then translate down by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(0,-1)$, and the curve extends left and downwards.

The radicand requires $-x\ge0$, so the domain is $(-\infty,0]$. At $x=0$, $y=-1$. Since $-\sqrt{-x}-1\le-1$, there is no $x$-intercept.

spec.description: Square-root curve extending left and down from (0,-1).

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ right by 1 unit and up by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(1,1)$, and the curve extends right and upwards.

The radicand requires $x-1\ge0$, so the domain is $[1,\infty)$. There is no $y$-intercept because $x=0$ is outside the domain, and no $x$-intercept because $y\ge1$.

spec.description: Square-root curve starting at (1,1), with neither axial intercept.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ left by 2 units and down by 2 units. The endpoint is $(-2,-2)$, and the curve extends right and upwards.

The radicand requires $x+2\ge0$, so the domain is $[-2,\infty)$.

At $x=0$, $y=\sqrt2-2$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{x+2}-2&=0\\\sqrt{x+2}&=2\\x+2&=4\\x&=2.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(2,0)$ and $(0,\sqrt2-2)$.

spec.description: Increasing square-root sketch with three individually labelled features; wider figure accommodates the exact surd label.

answer.short:
Endpoint $(-1,1)$; both axial intercepts $(0,0)$. Domain $[-1,\infty)$.

Reflect in the $x$-axis, translate left 1 unit, then up 1 unit.
answer.worked:
Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in the $x$-axis, translate left by 1 unit, then up by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(-1,1)$, and the curve extends right and downwards.

The radicand requires $x+1\ge0$, so the domain is $[-1,\infty)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-1+1=0$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}-\sqrt{x+1}+1&=0\\\sqrt{x+1}&=1\\x+1&=1\\x&=0.\end{align*}$$
Both axial intercepts are $(0,0)$.

spec.description: Decreasing square-root curve from (-1,1), crossing the origin.

answer.short:
Endpoint $(1,2)$; $y$-intercept $(0,3)$; no $x$-intercept. Domain $(-\infty,1]$.

Reflect in the $y$-axis, translate right 1 unit, then up 2 units.
answer.worked:
Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in the $y$-axis, translate right by 1 unit, then up by 2 units. The endpoint is $(1,2)$, and the curve extends left and upwards.

The radicand is $1-x$, requiring $x\le1$, so the domain is $(-\infty,1]$. At $x=0$, $y=\sqrt1+2=3$. Since $y\ge2$, there is no $x$-intercept.

spec.description: Square-root curve extending left and upwards from (1,2), passing through (0,3).

answer.short:
Endpoint and $x$-intercept $(-1,0)$; no $y$-intercept. Domain $(-\infty,-1]$.

Reflect in both axes, then translate left 1 unit.
answer.worked:
Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in both axes, then translate left by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(-1,0)$, and the curve extends left and downwards.

The radicand requires $-(x+1)\ge0$, so the domain is $(-\infty,-1]$.

At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}-\sqrt{-(x+1)}&=0\\-(x+1)&=0\\x&=-1.\end{align*}$$
There is no $y$-intercept because $x=0$ is outside the domain.

spec.description: Square-root curve extending left and down from (-1,0); no y-intercept.

answer.short:
Endpoint and $x$-intercept $(-2,0)$; $y$-intercept $(0,2)$. Domain $[-2,\infty)$.

Dilate horizontally by factor $\tfrac12$, then translate left 2 units.
answer.worked:
Write $y=\sqrt{2(x+2)}$. Dilate $y=\sqrt{x}$ horizontally by factor $\tfrac12$, then translate left by 2 units. The endpoint is $(-2,0)$, and the curve extends right and upwards.

The radicand requires $2x+4\ge0$, so the domain is $[-2,\infty)$. At $x=0$, $y=\sqrt4=2$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{2x+4}&=0\\2x+4&=0\\x&=-2.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(-2,0)$ and $(0,2)$.

spec.description: Horizontally compressed square-root curve from (-2,0), passing through (0,2).

answer.short:
Endpoint $(1,-2)$; $x$-intercept $(-3,0)$; $y$-intercept $(0,-1)$. Domain $(-\infty,1]$.

Reflect in the $y$-axis, translate right 1 unit, then down 2 units.
answer.worked:
Write $y=\sqrt{-(x-1)}-2$. Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ in the $y$-axis, translate right by 1 unit, then down by 2 units. The endpoint is $(1,-2)$, and the curve extends left and upwards.

The radicand requires $1-x\ge0$, so the domain is $(-\infty,1]$.

At $x=0$, $y=\sqrt1-2=-1$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{1-x}-2&=0\\\sqrt{1-x}&=2\\1-x&=4\\x&=-3.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(-3,0)$ and $(0,-1)$.

spec.description: Left-extending square-root curve from (1,-2), with both intercepts labelled.

answer.short:
Endpoint $(2,1)$; $x$-intercept $(\tfrac32,0)$; $y$-intercept $(0,-1)$. Domain $(-\infty,2]$.

Reflect in both axes, dilate horizontally by factor $\tfrac12$, translate right 2 units, then up 1 unit.
answer.worked:
Write $y=-\sqrt{-2(x-2)}+1$. From $y=\sqrt{x}$, reflect in both axes, dilate horizontally by factor $\tfrac12$, translate right by 2 units, then up by 1 unit. The endpoint is $(2,1)$, and the curve extends left and downwards.

The radicand requires $4-2x\ge0$, so the domain is $(-\infty,2]$.

At $x=0$, $y=-\sqrt4+1=-1$. At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}-\sqrt{4-2x}+1&=0\\\sqrt{4-2x}&=1\\4-2x&=1\\-2x&=-3\\x&=\tfrac32.\end{align*}$$
The axial intercepts are $(\tfrac32,0)$ and $(0,-1)$.

spec.description: Left-extending reflected and compressed square-root curve, with endpoint (2,1), x-intercept (3/2,0) and y-intercept (0,-1).
